item.title: 2170 Tabless Cell Development (Pilot Level)
item.description:
Project overview

  • Development task: Build a 2170 A sample using a tabless structure that connects the electrode and collector over a broad area instead of a conventional lead tab
  • Quality process: Company development flow based on IATF 16949: PROTO (A Sample) → PILOT (B and C Samples) → MP (CCB.PO) → SOP (mass production)
  • Completed gate: PROTO A-sample manufacturing and cell evaluation completed
  • Manufacturing constraint: No dedicated tabless equipment or jig; the route had to combine existing 4695 laser equipment with controlled manual work
  • Critical CTQs: Joint condition, internal laser entry and separator damage, insulation and shorts, IR, formation, capacity, and life
  • Direct scope: Early process design, 4M risk analysis, DFMEA, temporary 3D-printed jigs, laser and assembly conditions, sectioning, teardown, and cell evaluation
  • Final result: Compressed and separated failure modes across about 100 trials and confirmed build and functional feasibility through cell evaluation on five functional samples

IATF 16949-based development gates and current position

Quality stage Company sample or approval Technical objective Tabless project status
PROTO A Sample Confirm build feasibility, safety CTQs, and basic cell function for the new structure Completed — cell evaluation on five functional samples
PILOT B and C Samples Verify dedicated jigs/equipment, repeatability, inspection reproducibility, and productivity Transferred as follow-on design items
MP CCB.PO and C Sample Obtain technical production approval for the pilot conditions Follow-on gate
SOP Mass-production start Operate approved conditions in regular production Follow-on gate

The Tabless objective at PROTO was to build the new structure in actual cells and confirm safety and functional feasibility. The results were organized as equipment, jig, process, and inspection requirements for the subsequent PILOT B/C sample stages.
